reasoning_content:
The `clientIds` filter didn't seem to work (it returned all clients), but the response does contain the strassennamen client. Let's verify its configuration:

- clientId: strassennamen ✓
- enabled: true ✓
- publicClient: true ✓ (client authentication disabled)
- standardFlowEnabled: true ✓
- implicitFlowEnabled: true ✓
- directAccessGrantsEnabled: true ✓
- serviceAccountsEnabled: false ✓ (authorization not enabled)
- rootUrl: http://localhost:4200/ ✓
- adminUrl: http://localhost:4200/ ✓
- baseUrl: http://localhost:4200/ ✓
- redirectUris: ["http://localhost:4200/*", "http://localhost:5000/*"] ✓
- webOrigins: ["http://localhost:4200/*"] ✓
- post.logout.redirect_uris: "http://localhost:4200/*" ✓

Everything matches the guide. The client UUID is `fe46cc38-b90a-4bd4-ae89-c3075c2dc455`.

Next I'll check the client roles (app-access, editor) and user1's role mappings.

action.command: ADMIN_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:8080/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token" -d "grant_type=password&client_id=admin-cli&username=admin&password=admin" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])") && UUID="fe46cc38-b90a-4bd4-ae89-c3075c2dc455" && echo "=== Client roles ===" && curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/my-realm/clients/$UUID/roles" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print([r['name'] for r in json.load(sys.stdin)])" && echo "=== user1 client role mappings ===" && UID2=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/my-realm/users?username=user1" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]['id'])") && curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "http://localhost:8080/admin/realms/my-realm/users/$UID2/role-mappings/clients/$UUID" | python3 -c "import sys,json; print([r['name'] for r in json.load(sys.stdin)])"
